name: Santase 66: Offline Card Game
subtitle: Schnapsen against a strong AI
promotionalText: The classic trick-taking game against five computer opponents, from a friendly beginner to a Grandmaster. No internet, sign-up or ads, in English and Bulgarian.
description:
Santase 66 is the classic two-player card game, known across the Balkans as Santase, in Austria and Germany as Schnapsen, and elsewhere as 66 or Sechsundsechzig. Play it against a genuinely strong computer, without an internet connection, registration or ads.

FIVE COMPUTER OPPONENTS
• From Lucky, who plays at random, to the Grandmaster, who simulates thousands of deals before every move.
• Every opponent runs entirely on your device.
• Each one shows its rating, so you can see how far you have come.

PLAY AND LEARN
• Classic rules: a 24-card deck, marriages of 20 and 40, exchanging the trump nine, closing the talon, and first to 11 game points.
• Hints that suggest a card, an exchange or a close.
• Badges on your cards that show when a lead would announce a marriage.
• The last trick stays on view, and the rules are built in.
• Three game speeds, with settings for assists and vibration.

TWO PLAYERS, ONE DEVICE
Pass the phone to a friend for a game against each other. Each player's cards stay hidden until they are ready.

FOLLOW YOUR PROGRESS
See your rating, wins, losses, streaks and completed game history. These statistics track your games against the computer and are saved in the app.

ENGLISH AND BULGARIAN
Switch languages from the home screen or settings.

PLAY WITH PEOPLE
The online-play button opens the separate ednaigra.com website in your browser. The website needs an internet connection; online multiplayer is not built into the app.

No ads or in-app purchases. Offline games require no account.
